TASK: F3e2 (GF4, GF5; P8.3): the Studio reviews a recorded unit, assigns its code and issues its card
through the registry. All three parts are done and committed. Nothing was written to the demo: every
step that stores is mocked in the screenshots, from R3's stored exchanges where one exists.
WORKS: 1. Review and assign (fac523f9). The block of a recorded unit without a code reads its reviews (GET)
and offers "Review and assign code". The dialog shows what is decided, asks for a reason (required,
empty), and "Record review" sends the capture and then the review: operation assign, no location for
a source-stated unit. "Assign code" sends the assignment with the four values of that review. The
code is shown only once the canonical record states it. An unused review the registry already lists
is offered for assignment as it is. A unit with a code shows no review action.
2. Issue a card (534e3461). The Cards block offers "Issue new revision" when a listed card is valid
now under an unchanged snapshot, otherwise "Issue card". One required "Valid until" (local date and
time, empty; a past value or one more than 24 hours ahead is refused in the form with "Use an expiry
within the next 24 hours." before anything is sent) and, for a first card, one required "Why this
citation is included" (empty, at most 2,048 characters). The dialog says before Prepare that Prepare
is not a dry run. Prepare runs capture, entries, plan create, confirm, execute and preview, and the
same instant goes to the plan, the preview and the card. Afterwards the dialog shows the entry, the
plan id and the packet receipt as answered, and the preview's mode, revision and rows in the
answered order. Only "Issue card" sends generate; the cards are then read again and the dialog
closes on the listed row. An entry answered as not includable is shown with its reason code and
Prepare stops there. For a revision Prepare reads the listed card and the preview and stores
nothing; the dialog says so.
3. Drafts (1924e344). Of the two ways the task allows I took the smaller: the map inspector links to
the recorded unit ("Open recorded unit") and does not open the dialogs itself. The link lands on the
unit block, which is scrolled to and takes the focus. The inspector's header reads Assigned from the
canonical record, else the review status of the ledger; it reads and writes nothing in the browser
store. useRecordReview is removed and recordReview is no longer exported. The draft verify page is
untouched.
4. Both dialogs: each request is sent once per click and the button is disabled while it is in
flight. A refusal is stated with the server's code and words and the dialog stays open with what was
typed. After no answer the dialog says the result is unknown and offers "Read the record again",
never a resend of its own; for a lost card request a new listed row means the card exists, otherwise
the officer may send the same request with the same key.
5. Found by my own review after the part commits and fixed: the field took the focus before the
dialog noted its opener, so the focus did not return on a second open (in 534e3461); the expiry was
printed twice after Prepare (8b16e4a3); the inspector drew an empty action bar for a space with no
action (a3338518); two literal text sizes where tokens exist (8f74a09a).

DESIGN: One way to send a command: features/identity/outcome.ts states refusals with refusalOf of
features/review/candidates/commands.ts and adds the one distinction these flows need, refused or
unknown. Request bodies are built by pure functions (assignment.ts, issue.ts) and typed from
@ulpin/api-client; no response shape is written by hand.
Prepare is one sequence in prepare.ts that names the step it stopped at. A lost answer in a step
that stores is an unknown outcome; in a step that only reads it is a failed read.
One snapshot is captured per record revision per open dialog and reused by later Prepare clicks. The
two dialogs share no state, so the card dialog always captures its own.
The rows of the card are printed by a small new component: the existing card facts take a browser
workflow, not the preview's rows. A row that is not available keeps its value and shows its state
"Valid until" is typed in the browser's zone and shown after Prepare as the registry answered it,
once. The task's form sentence is used as the hint and as the refusal.
After a refused assignment the dialog offers "Record a new review"; after a refused card request
